description: Large language models are evolving from answer engines into conversational partners that shape decisions by asking their own questions. Research comparing more than 1,600 executives with 13 leading models finds that AI systems use markedly different question mixes than human leaders, often overemphasizing interpretive analysis while underweighting productive and subjective questions. Because each question type surfaces different information, these imbalances can create blind spots, skew discussions, and subtly steer outcomes. Models also vary widely from one another, meaning tool choice matters. Managers must be deliberate about when and how they use inquiry-driven AI; compare outputs across systems; actively probe for missing perspectives, especially execution and stakeholder concerns; and retain final judgment. Treat AI’s questions as inputs to guide thinking, not as substitutes for leadership.
title: The Risks of Letting AI Direct Conversations
